summary: Trịnh Xuân Thuận works in philosophy and other fields. He studied at the California Institute of Technology (~1967–1970) and Princeton University (~1970–1974), and held a post at the University of Virginia around 1976.

Tse-fu Kuan works in Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich (1999–2004), conducted postdoctoral research at National Cheng Kung University, and held a post at Yuan Ze University (attested 2015).

Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Ganden Monastery, earning a Geshe Lharampa degree. He held a post at Ganden Jangtse Monastery and taught the 14th Dalai Lama, Alexander Berzin, Joseph Loizzo, and Thubten Chodron.

Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang was a Tibetology and linguistics scholar who studied at Panjab University, Tibetan Children's Village, and the University of Glasgow (1987). He served as headmaster at Tibetan Children's Village and became Instructor in Tibetan at Oxford in 2001.

Tsering Shakya is a Tibetology and history scholar who earned his BA, MPhil, and PhD at SOAS University of London. He was a research fellow at SOAS (1999–2002), taught at Oxford, and joined the University of British Columbia (~2007).

Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at the Young Lamas Home School. He served as master of Vajrayana ceremonies at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling Monastery (~1976–2020) and was a board member of Rangjung Yeshe Shenpen.

Tsoknyi Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Khampagar Monastery and under teachers including Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse, and Tulku Urgyen. He held a post at Tergar Osel Ling Monastery and founded Pundarika Foundation.

Tsuguhito Takeuchi was a Tibetology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Indiana University Bloomington (PhD 1994) under Christopher I. Beckwith and others. He was Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~2001–2017).

Tsugunari Kubo was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He served as President of Reiyukai (~1970–1993, ~1996–2013) and President of the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1995–2019).

Tsukasa Mizushima is an Indology and history scholar who earned his bachelor's, master's, and doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1979–1995) and the University of Tokyo (1997–2018), where he is professor emeritus.

Tsultrim Allione is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who earned a master's degree at Antioch University. She studied under Apho Rinpoche, Chögyam Trungpa, Namkhai Norbu, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Kalu Rinpoche, and founded Tara Mandala in 1993.

Tsultrim Gyatso is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held posts as senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as abbot at Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987).

Tsultrim Kelsang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the International Buddhist Association (attested 1973), Otani University as lecturer (attested 1984) and professor (attested 1999–2002), and Ryukoku University as a researcher in 2015.

Tsuneki Nishiwaki is a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1963–1967). He held posts at Doshisha University (~1974–1990) and as professor at Kyoto University (~1990–2007).

Tsung-i Jao was a Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Shantou Jinshan Middle School (~1929–1930). He held posts at the University of Hong Kong (~1952–1968), National University of Singapore (~1968–1973), Yale (~1970–1971), and EPHE (~1978–1979).
Tsutomu Hatai was an Indology scholar who succeeded Hiroshi Maruyama and served as president of the Ayurveda Research Society (attested 1987).

Tsutomu Kubo was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University (1929–1946), and Toyo University (~1949–1954).

Tsutomu Yamaguchi is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Hokkaido University. He held posts as a collaborative researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2015 and 2026).

Tsuyoshi Yokoyama works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and served as a specially appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2017).
Tsyben Zhamtsarano was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1902 and headed the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.
